newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton ends lower in slow, technical trade.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton ends lower in slow, technical trade.

text.p: NYCE cotton closed a thinly-traded session weaker, as prices continued to retreat from the 15-week highs reached last week.
Traders blamed losses on local liquidation following NYCE's weekly spec/hedge report, which showed the speculators to be holding a 21.3 percent net long position.
The benchmark contract closed down 0.29 cent at 76.83 cents per lb, having ranged from 77.35 to 76.76 cents. The rest of the board settled 0.32 to 0.20 cent lower.
Resistance in December remained at 77.70-77.95 cents, and support at 76.40-76.10 cents.
An estimated 8,500 lots changed hands on the day, compared with Monday's official 6,413 lots.
A lack of news contributed to today's subdued tone following Monday's uninspiring U.S. Department of Agriculture planted area estimate of 14.0 million acres, analysts said.
They said the reduction from the initial 14.485 million acre estimate had already been filtered into the market, and added that prices could trade rangebound without any fundamental news.

"For December futures to push 79.00 cents and higher, a serious threat to supply will be needed," Carl Anderson, a cotton marketing specialist with Texas A & M University, said in a weekly comment. "A good foreign crop could weaken the market."
Traders are looking for slack exports on Thursday, when the USDA issues its weekly export and sales report.
NYCE will be closed Friday for the Fourth of July holiday, and will reopen on Monday, July 7.
